paper_title: Evidencing Excellent Thermal- and Photostability for Single-Component Organic Solar Cells with Inherently Built-In Microstructure
source_file: /home/wzfeng/MySearch/PhotoRag/MD/Advanced Energy Materials - 2019 - He - Evidencing Excellent Thermal‐ and Photostability for Single‐Component Organic Solar/auto/Advanced Energy Materials - 2019 - He - Evidencing Excellent Thermal‐ and Photostability for Single‐Component Organic Solar.md

knowledge_points.content: SCP3 is a double-cable conjugated polymer consisting of a diketopyrrolopyrrole (DPP)-based backbone as the donor and pendant perylene bisimide (PBI) units as the electron acceptor, connected via flexible alkyl side chains.
knowledge_points.evidence: In 2017, Li et al. developed a double-cable polymer (called SCP3) using diketopyrrolopyrrole (DPP)-based backbone and pendant perylene bisimide (PBI) as electron acceptor, connected with flexible alkyl side chains.

knowledge_points.content: Optimized single-component organic solar cells based on the double-cable polymer SCP3 achieve a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of approximately 2.6%.
knowledge_points.evidence: The current density-voltage (J-V) curves for SCP3-based solar cells under both light and dark conditions are exhibited in Figure 1, showing an efficiency of around 2.6% which is in accordance with the values reported in literature.

knowledge_points.content: SCP3-based organic solar cells demonstrate exceptional thermal stability, maintaining 100% of their initial power conversion efficiency after being heated at 160 °C for over 400 hours in a nitrogen atmosphere.
knowledge_points.evidence: Particularly, the SCOsCs exhibit ultrahigh long-term thermal stability with 100% PCE remaining after heating at temperature up to 160 °C for over 400 h, indicating an excellent candidate for extremely rugged applications.

knowledge_points.content: The superior stability of single-component organic solar cells compared to bulk-heterojunction (BHJ) systems is attributed to the covalent linkage between donor and acceptor units, which prevents large-scale phase de-mixing and morphological evolution under thermal or light stress.
knowledge_points.evidence: Large scale de-mixing was prevented in such a design, and as a result we found an exceptional thermal stability for a solution-processed OSC... the double-cable design, relying on a covalently linked and therefore inherently fixed microstructure, is a generic way to overcome microstructure induced burn-in degradation.

knowledge_points.content: The temperature coefficient of the open-circuit voltage (VOC) for SCP3-based solar cells is approximately -2.1 mV/K, which is comparable to the values observed for crystalline silicon and GaAs solar cells.
knowledge_points.evidence: SCP3-based solar cells displayed a comparable temperature coefficient of -2.1 mV K^-1, which was comparable to Si and GaAs solar cells (around -2.1 -1.7 mV K^-1).

knowledge_points.content: Transient photovoltage (TPV) and charge extraction (CE) measurements reveal a recombination order of approximately 2.8 to 3.0 for both fresh and aged SCP3-based solar cells, indicating second-order recombination in the presence of energetic disorder.
knowledge_points.evidence: We calculated a recombination order of 2.8 for fresh and 2.9, 3.0, and 2.9 for aged SCP3-based solar cells... These values presented second-order recombination (R = 2) behavior in the presence of significant energetic disorder.

knowledge_points.content: Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) and modulated DSC (m-DSC) of the SCP3 polymer show no melting peaks, phase changes, or clear glass transitions between 50 °C and 200 °C, indicating a highly crystalline and thermally stable material.
knowledge_points.evidence: The differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) curves of SCP3... exhibited no melting peaks and no phase change between 50 and 200 °C. Besides, no clear glass transition was observed from the temperature modulated DSC (m-DSC) measurement, resulting from the high crystallinity nature of SCP3 material.

knowledge_points.content: The performance of SCP3-based solar cells remains stable under simultaneous stress of 90 °C and 1 sun illumination for 300 hours, with less than 5% variation in VOC and Fill Factor (FF).
knowledge_points.evidence: We further investigated the stability of SCP3-based solar cells under 90 °C & illumination. As displayed in Figure 2C, the efficiency remained still unaffected, with almost identical VOC and FF values as the initial ones (less than 5% variation).

knowledge_points.content: Optimal performance for SCP3-based solar cells in an inverted structure is achieved by implementing a high-temperature thermal annealing step at 200 °C for 10 minutes prior to the evaporation of the top silver electrode.
knowledge_points.evidence: With an inverted structure (Figure 1), the performance of SCP3-based OSCs was optimized by a thermal annealing step at 200 °C for 10 min before evaporation of the top electrode.

knowledge_points.content: While the SCP3 active layer is stable at 200 °C, the overall device performance decreases at this temperature due to the penetration of the silver top electrode into the active layer.
knowledge_points.evidence: As indicated by DSC curves, SCP3 material should be fairly stable at 200 °C; while from the picture of silver electrodes after heating at 200 °C for 1 h... it is obvious that the top electrode became foggy, indicating silver penetrating into active layer and thus decreasing the performance.

knowledge_points.content: The charge carrier mobility of fresh SCP3-based solar cells, as determined by Photo-CELIV, is approximately 4.93 x 10^-5 cm^2 V^-1 s^-1, and it remains relatively stable after degradation under various conditions.
knowledge_points.evidence: As calculated from the Photo-CELIV traces in Figure S11... the charge carrier mobility of fresh SCP3-based solar cells was 4.93 x 10^-5 cm^2 V^-1 s^-1... the extraction peak (t_max) was hardly shifted and broadened after degradation.

knowledge_points.content: The high crystallinity of the SCP3 polymer is a key factor in its resistance to the formation of thermal- or light-induced trap states, which helps maintain stable photovoltaic performance.
knowledge_points.evidence: It is plausible that this peculiar morphology with high crystallinity is a chief aspect of its enhanced stability, which is consistent with earlier work, showing that crystalline polymers are less prone to thermal- or light-induced traps.
